title: Human persuasion is weak without the divine argument; Spirit's efficacy; Christians would rather die than deny
pass_a_gloss: 15. And in this manner one must proceed against atheists and gentiles: but because these proofs for the most part rest only on human authority and testimony, they can produce in the intellect only an assent of human persuasion, which is much inferior and weaker than Christian faith, unless a divine argument and weight from the sacred letters is added. XIV. These things concerning human arguments by which the Christian religion is made credible: there follows the divine argument, which is the efficacy of the Holy Spirit implanted in sacred Scripture, by which its force toward persuading is elevated and strengthened, and breathed into the heart of the reader. 1. Christians assent so firmly that they prefer to die rather than deny its divine truth. 2. This assent depends proximately and through itself from nowhere else than from scripture itself as autopistos, as is clear from 1 Thess. 2:13.
pass_b_english: Proceed against atheists this way. Yet these proofs mostly rest only on human authority and produce only human persuasion — far weaker than Christian faith, unable to persevere in serious contest unless the divine argument from the sacred letters is added (Bellarmine, Bullinger, Valencia, Ficino, Mornay, Grotius).

XIV. So much for human arguments. Next the divine argument: the Holy Spirit's efficacy implanted in Sacred Scripture, by which its persuasive power is raised and breathed into the reader's heart — for which Christians receive it in the spiritual struggle with firm, unmoved, world-conquering, utterly divine assent.

1. Christians who watch for their soul's salvation assent so firmly that they would rather die than deny Scripture's divine truth. 2. This assent depends proximately on nothing else than Scripture itself as self-attesting (αὐτόπιστος), as [[1 Thessalonians 2:13 >> Bible:1 Thessalonians 2:13]] shows: they received the word not as a human word but as the word of God.
source_text:
Probationes humanae persuasionem humanam gignunt, fide Christiana infirmiorem, nisi divinum argumentum a sacris literis accedat.

XIV. Sequitur argumentum divinum: Spiritus sancti efficacia sacrae Scripturae indita… 1. Christiani malunt mori quam veritatem negare. 2. Assensus ab ipsa scriptura αὐτοπίστῳ (1. Thess. 2.13).
